title: Grade 4 Social Studies — How State and Local Government Work
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on Ohio, General Assembly, governor, services.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What is the capital of Ohio?
Who leads Ohio's executive branch?
choices: the chief of a local fire department
the speaker of the U.S. House

questions.question: Which group passes state laws in Ohio?
What are the two chambers of Ohio's General Assembly?
Which branch decides cases under state law?
Which concern is usually handled closest to a small town?
choices: how to represent the United States abroad
whether to print a dollar bill
where to put signs on a town street

questions.question: Which example belongs to Ohio state government?
choices: maintaining state highways through the state transportation department

questions.question: Which group could pass a city rule about parking on a city-owned street?
What is a reason a state has counties?
choices: to set a different national currency in each area
to make each part a separate country
to organize some services and government closer to residents

questions.question: What document sets up Ohio's state government?
choices: the United States Declaration of Independence

questions.question: What is one job of a state court?
Which question should you take first to a city or township office?
choices: Who runs the federal space program?
Who handles a damaged sign on this local street?
Who negotiated a treaty with France?

questions.question: Which is one purpose of a public budget?
choices: record how long a street is
name a new state bird each year
plan how tax money and other funds will be used

questions.question: Which level usually has authority over rules for Ohio driver's licenses?
Who elects Ohio's governor?
How can Ohio residents learn what their state legislators are considering?
choices: look only at a street map
read bills and schedules from the General Assembly

questions.question: Which is most likely a responsibility of local government in a city?
Why are different branches given different jobs?
choices: to give every office the same tasks
to end the need for any laws
to ensure only one person decides everything

questions.question: Which correctly compares a state governor and a city mayor?
choices: Both officials work only for the federal courts.
A governor leads the state executive branch; a mayor often leads a city government.
A mayor leads all states; a governor leads one school.
A city's mayor serves as the governor of Ohio.

questions.question: A resident wants the state to change a state law. Who is an appropriate person to contact?
choices: the owner of the nearest store
